status: Focused LTO, comment and packaging checks pass. Full RPM qualification remains required. No upload.
root_cause: External -flto=auto came after Node GYP flags and bypassed configure enable_lto. The top-level assembly object has no PushAllRegistersAndIterateStack symbol in its GCC LTO symbol table. Node's existing --enable-lto configuration compiles its assembly-containing V8 target natively and enables LTO elsewhere. The recipe now routes distribution LTO requests through that configuration, preserving hardening flags.
scope: Only LTO flag routing and six comment chains change from candidate4. Approved -Wno-error=return-type remains visible. No assembly, C++ runtime behavior, warning suppression, or global LTO disabling is introduced.

checks.negative_link: Exact missing symbol reproduced using unchanged upstream assembly in an archive and an LTO caller.
checks.positive_link: Native assembly plus LTO caller links and passes 1360000 stack callbacks natively and under Valgrind.
checks.generated_commands: Actual configure/make commands prove native assembly-containing target, LTO-enabled Node target, and all distribution hardening flags.
checks.comments: Six original warnings reproduced; corrected comments preprocess to identical tokens with warnings as errors.

limitations: First configure-control parser mistakenly included make's command-cache printf; corrected parser checks only actual g++ command lines.
Candidate4 did not reach RPM tests; its new allocator/string-operation diagnostics require review on the correctly configured full build.
Focused stack control is x86_64; ARM requires native OBS and installed qualification.
